topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the final lecture by outlining the learning objectives and scope of cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional local and systemic cancer interventions alongside the toxicities and multidrug resistance mechanisms associated with cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that selectively target cancer cells by exploiting hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors against oncogenic kinases and managing the emergence of gatekeeper mutations, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the design, mechanism of action, and clinical application of naked monoclonal antibodies and toxin-linked antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for anti-tumor immune surveillance and the development of cellular and receptor-targeted immunotherapies, including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broader therapeutic challenges, mortality trends, and ethical considerations surrounding the integration of novel targeted agents alongside proven combination regimens.
